title: Adjacency encoding cost bound
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,s,C$ be nonnegative integers. Write $Q$ for its state set, and let $A=|Q|+6k+5$ and $T=2^k(2|Q|+2)^{	ext{?}}$—more precisely, $T=2^k\,|\mathrm{Option}(Q)\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\times(\mathrm{Fin}(k)\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool}))|\,2^{3k+7}(3k+8)$. If $A\le C$, then the cost of the concatenation of the input-equality CNF and transition CNF is at most $(6+T)C(s+n+2)^{k+2}$. Here the cost of a CNF is the sum, over its clauses, of one plus the clause length.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Boolean-alphabet Turing machine
caveat: The transition coefficient is rendered directly from its formal definition; the unusual cardinality expression is left in set notation.
